Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 22, verse 78:

His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying:

﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty; the religion of your father Abraham. He named you "Muslims" before, and in this [Revelation], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer, give zakah, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector; how excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper!﴾

A group said: This is a verse in which Allah, may He be exalted, commanded striving in His cause, which is fighting the disbelievers. Another group said: It is more general than that, encompassing the striving of the self (jihad al-nafs), the striving against the disbelievers, the striving against the oppressors, and other things. Allah commanded His servants to do that for the sake of Allah with the striving due to Him.

The Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

The generality is good. It clarifies that the customary usage of the term requires jihad in the way of Allah. Hibat Allah (p-276) and others said: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿with the striving due to Him﴾, and His saying in the other [verse]: ﴿with the piety due to Him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102], are abrogated (mansukh) by the lightening to [what is within] capacity (al-istita'ah).

The Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

The meaning of capacity (al-istita'ah) in these commands is what is intended from the very beginning. The obligation to reach the utmost extent was never established as a fixed legal ruling, so it cannot be said that it was abrogated by the lightening. Their use of the term abrogation (naskh) in this context is not precise. "Ijtaba-kum" means: chose you.

His, may He be exalted, saying ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾ means: any constriction. He intends: in the legislation of the religion, for it is a pure monotheistic religion (hanifiyyah), tolerant (samhah), unlike the hardships of the Children of Israel and others. Rather, it contains repentance, expiations, dispensations, and similar things whose number is great. "Al-harajah" is the thick, intertwined, constricted tree. The lifting of difficulty is valid for the majority of this community and for whoever keeps to the path of the Law. As for the highwaymen, thieves, and those subject to the prescribed punishments, difficulty is upon them, and they have brought it upon themselves by abandoning the religion. There is no greater difficulty in the Law than obligating a man to stand against two in the way of Allah, may He be exalted; yet with sound certainty and firm resolve it is not a difficulty.

His saying "millata" (the religion of) is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb whose estimate is: rather, He made it, or something similar of verbs of urging. Al-Farra' said: it is in the accusative by the deletion of the particle "ka-" (like), as if he said: "like the religion of". It was also said: it is accusative as the verbal noun is made accusative. His saying "Huwa sammakum" (He named you): Ibn Zayd said: the pronoun refers to Abraham, and the reference is to His saying: ﴿and from our offspring a Muslim community for You﴾ [al-Baqarah: 128]. Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, and Mujahid said: the pronoun refers to Allah, may He be exalted. "Min qabl" (before) means: in the earlier scriptures. "Wa fi hadha" (and in this) means: in the Qur'an. This expression weakens the view of those who say the pronoun refers to Abraham, and it can only be directed to it with an omitted, resumptive clause in the speech (p-277). His, may He be exalted, saying ﴿that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ means: by conveying [the message]. His saying ﴿and you may be witnesses over the people﴾ means: by conveying to them their messengers' message, as your Prophet has informed you.

Al-Tabari transmitted with his chain to Qatadah that he said: This community was given what no one was given except a prophet. It was said to the Prophet: "You are a witness over your community," and it was said to this community: ﴿and you may be witnesses over the people﴾. It was said to the Prophet: "There is no hardship upon you," and it was said to this community: ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾. It was said to the Prophet: "Ask and you will be given," and it was said to this community: ﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60].

Then, may He be exalted, commanded that the obligatory prayer be established and maintained with all its limits, and that zakah be paid, as He has bestowed favour upon you, so do such-and-such. Then He commanded holding fast to Allah, may He be exalted, that is, clinging to Him, sincerity toward Him, seeking deliverance from Him, and abandoning reliance on anyone else. "Al-mawla" in this verse means: the one whose help and protection are yours. The rest of the verse is clear.

The tafsir of Surah al-Hajj is complete, by the praise and help of Allah, may He be exalted.
